Wait, looking at the image, the buttons are:
- Horizontal row: B, w, B, w, w (black, white, black, white, white)
- Vertical row: B, w, B, w, w (black, white, black, white, white)
So both rows are the same pattern: B, w, B, w, w.
This is interesting. Maybe the goal is to make both rows match? Let me try setting them to the same pattern.
Actually, they're already the same pattern. But the level didn't complete.
Let me try a different approach. Maybe the goal is to make the buttons match the yellow shapes in some way. The person shape has a "head" and "body", and the U shape has "sides" and "bottom".
Actually, let me think about this more carefully. The person shape could be represented as:
- Top row: wide (head)
- Bottom row: narrow (body)
The U shape could be represented as:
- Top row: narrow (sides)
- Bottom row: wide (bottom)
So maybe the buttons need to be set to:
- Horizontal row: wide, narrow, wide, narrow, wide (or some pattern)
- Vertical row: narrow, wide, narrow, wide, narrow (or some pattern)
Let me try setting the buttons to match the yellow shapes more directly. The person shape is 4 pixels wide and 4 pixels tall. The U shape is 6 pixels wide and 5 pixels tall.
Actually, I'm overcomplicating this. Let me just try all possible button patterns systematically. Since there are 10 buttons (5 horizontal + 5 vertical), and each can be black or white, there are 2^10 = 1024 possible combinations. But many of them are symmetric or equivalent.
Let me try a simpler approach: set all buttons to the same color (all black or all white) and see if that works.
Actually, I already tried all black and it didn't work. Let me try all white.
